name: Endless-accelerando (Risset rhythm) illusion for cinematic tension: the same pattern at double speed fading out and at half speed fading in while tempo automates to double, dropped subdivisions (fade every other note of a six-pulse group as tempo doubles), half-speed (3/4) and third-speed (6/8) copies forming a 3:2 hemiola fractal, voices swapping roles across cycles, and a long note gliding slowly against a sustained pitch
goal: Make a rhythm that seems to speed up forever without ever getting too fast, the rhythmic version of a Shepard tone. Basic form: play a pattern, the same pattern at double speed fading out above it, and at half speed fading in below it, while tempo automates up to double; then loop. In a track: take a group of six steady pulses and, as tempo rises toward double, fade every second note until it disappears, so at double tempo you hear the original rhythm again. Layer the same six-pulse pattern at half speed (three strong pulses, 3/4 feel) and at one-third speed (two pulses, 6/8 feel) for a 3:2 hemiola; give each layer its own dropped-subdivision transformation and fade layers in and out across cycles so the ear never locks onto one, and let a voice that played the 2-pulse role take the 3-pulse role in the next cycle. Double tempo per cycle (150 → 300 → 600 in the video) and reset where the DAW tempo ceiling is reached. Add tension with a long note rising slowly against a sustained pitch, passing every dissonance. Fits Polyrhythm Studio as tempo-scaled lanes with per-lane gain automation.

source.title: Recreating The Impossible Rhythm Illusion In "The Odyssey" Soundtrack
source.transcript_note: Analysis and recreation; course/Patreon promotion dropped.

prerequisites: DAW with tempo automation and per-track volume automation, or Web Audio: a lookahead scheduler whose tempo ramps exponentially to 2× per cycle, with per-layer GainNode ramps and per-note velocity scaling for dropped subdivisions (implementation note)
Percussive or plucked voices, a sustained pad and a gliding voice

inputs.name: base_pattern
inputs.description: Group of six steady pulses (or any short pattern)

inputs.name: layers
inputs.description: Speed ratios: 2×, 1×, ½ (3/4 feel), ⅓ (6/8 feel)

outputs.name: risset_rhythm
outputs.description: Tempo and gain automation that loops seamlessly

outputs.name: tension_layer
outputs.description: Long rising glissando against a drone

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
The loop point only works if, at doubled tempo, the faded layers exactly match the starting state; check levels at both ends.
Some DAWs cap tempo (999 BPM in the video); reset tempo at a cycle boundary instead of doubling past it.
The presenter admits not fully decoding the original; this is his recreation. Composer/film named only as reference; no audio copied. Course and Patreon promotion dropped.

steps.action: Build the basic form: one pattern, a double-speed copy fading out over the cycle, a half-speed copy fading in, and tempo automated to double over the same cycle. Loop it.
steps.expect: A constant sense of acceleration with a seamless loop

steps.action: Dropped subdivisions: play a group of six pulses; as tempo rises toward double, ramp down the level of every second note until silent.
steps.expect: At doubled tempo the rhythm sounds like the original again

steps.action: Add the same six-pulse pattern at half speed (three strong pulses, 3/4 feel) and at one-third speed (two pulses, 6/8 feel).
steps.expect: A 3-against-2 hemiola under the main line

steps.action: Apply the dropped-subdivision fade to each layer in turn, staggering them, and fade whole layers in and out across cycles; let a voice move from the 2-pulse role to the 3-pulse role in the next section.
steps.expect: The listener can't follow any single layer; the illusion continues

steps.action: Automate tempo doubling cycle by cycle (e.g. 150 → 300 → 600) and reset to the start tempo at a cycle boundary when you hit the tempo ceiling, with fades placed in those transition zones.
steps.expect: Endless acceleration over a long track

steps.action: Add tension: a long note gliding slowly upward against a sustained pitch, plus heavily reverberated vocal or texture layers.
steps.expect: A stressful, constantly sliding dissonance that matches the rhythm

verification: At the loop or reset point there is no audible jump in perceived tempo or density.
At the end of a cycle, the faded every-other-note group matches the starting rhythm.
Soloing the ½ and ⅓ speed layers shows 3 and 2 strong pulses per bar respectively.
Skipping between sections reveals the actual tempo is not monotonic, while listening straight through feels constantly faster.
